audit.why: EVEN 6/10 fits 53.44% across 1658 games. The mirror rates the lane 8/10 from Nautilus's side, which is the inverse of the same read, so no change is needed here.
audit.corrected: Difficulty held at 6/10 — deliberately not copying the mirror's 8/10, since that number belongs to the other side.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 3 and 4 read Skill in both layers; the packet has Poppy at 4-5 and Nautilus at 6, and whys[4] already says the lead is his while his ultimate is up.
audit.why: Depth Charge (120/100/80s) is a genuine level-6 flip, and whys[3] argues Poppy wins the 4-5 window next to a Skill row.
audit.corrected: Rows 3 and 4 flipped as one atomic paired group in both layers: Skill, Poppy, Poppy, Poppy, Nautilus, Poppy, Poppy — matching the packet and the mirror. Row 4 rating moved to 3/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: Keeper's Verdict is a channel, and Nautilus holds three separate ways to cancel it — Staggering Blow (P) on his first auto, Dredge Line (Q) on 14/13/12/11/10s, and Depth Charge (R). None of this is on the page. Titan's Wrath's shield is also never mentioned.
audit.why: Poppy's ultimate is described as her win condition while the enemy who most reliably deletes it goes unnamed; and committing burst into a 12s-cooldown shield wastes the whole trade.
audit.corrected: Channel-cancel warning added to the level-6 row and the don'ts; Titan's Wrath named as the thing to force out before committing.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeats 'W any dash he tries — his mobility is a suggestion' as the trading rule.
audit.why: Dredge Line is not flagged as a dash in Riot's data — it pulls Nautilus toward terrain, and toward a champion it pulls both together. The concrete punish window is the 14s hook cooldown at rank 1, not a dash-stop.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the real cooldown window and the shield read.

edits.before: Passive shield trades + Q zone control win early. Identify how Nautilus contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Two one-ability tanks with no combo yet. Note that his first auto on you roots via Staggering Blow, so do not linger in auto range.

edits.before: W deletes his dash mid-flight — hold it like a parry. Only take the trade when Nautilus's Dredge Line is down.
edits.after: Your wall-stun arrives before his engage does — E him into terrain and Hammer Shock the ground, after Dredge Line has missed.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Nautilus must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Full kit online — your strongest early window. Keep the wave near you so a Dredge Line miss leaves him inside your 475 E range.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Dredge Line's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: The lane-control window: a missed Dredge Line is down 14-11s — engage inside it, and force Titan's Wrath out before you spend your damage.

edits.before: Keeper’s Verdict punts the fight’s biggest threat across the map. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Nautilus's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Depth Charge is point-and-click on 120s and chains into his hook. It also cancels Keeper's Verdict outright — never channel while his R is up.

edits.before: Iceborn Gauntlet is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Dredge Line's cooldown.
edits.after: Iceborn Gauntlet is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, inside the Dredge Line downtime.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Nautilus carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Neither tank out-scales the other, so the side lane stays yours wherever terrain is close. Nautilus carry threat 7/10 in fights, not duels.

edits.before: E Nautilus into a wall when his answer is down, Q the zone under him, and W any dash he tries — his mobility is a suggestion.
edits.after: E Nautilus into a wall once Dredge Line has missed, Q the zone under him, and make Titan's Wrath's 12s shield burn before your damage lands.

edits.before: E Nautilus into a wall when his answer is down, Q the zone under him, and W any dash he tries — his mobility is a suggestion.
edits.after: E Nautilus into a wall once Dredge Line has missed, Q the zone under him, and make Titan's Wrath's 12s shield burn before your damage lands.

edits.before: That is Nautilus's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Any of his CC cancels Keeper's Verdict — channel only after Dredge Line is spent.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Staggering Blow roots off his first auto on you — leave auto range after a trade.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay in your favor — your Q percent-HP damage scales off his HP, not your gold, so every trade chips him faster than his flat base damage hurts you. At 6 respect his R: it's a point-and-click knockup that chains into his Q hook and E, so it's his one real all-in window. Don't facecheck or step up when his ultimate is available; once it's down, you reclaim the lane and keep pressing the wall-stun.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay in your favor — your Q chunks his fat HP bar regardless of gold, and a missed Dredge Line leaves him 14-11s without an engage, so that is your window. At 6 respect his R: point-and-click on 120s, it chains into hook and Riptide, and it cancels your Keeper's Verdict channel on contact. Don't facecheck while his ultimate is up; once it's down, reclaim the lane and keep pressing the wall-stun.

edits.before: His R is his power moment — a single-target knockup that sets up his Q hook and E follow-up, so respect his all-in the instant his ultimate is up.
edits.after: Depth Charge is his power moment — a 120s point-and-click knockup that sets up hook and Riptide, and it cancels your Keeper's Verdict channel outright.

notes: UNVERIFIED, LEFT UNTOUCHED — the same two claims the mirror flagged: (1) that Steadfast Presence grounds or eats Dredge Line (Poppy's W stops dashes; Nautilus's Q is not flagged a dash in Riot's data, it is a pull), asserted in wants.you[1], whys[5], whys[6] and late; (2) that Hammer Shock deals percent-current-health damage, asserted in whys[3], whys[5], spikes[2] and mid — no percentHealth flag exists in Poppy's kit and Riot's text mentions none. Both need a human ruling before rewriting; I removed the dash-stop only from the generic trading boilerplate where a verified replacement existed. Rows 3 and 4 flipped as one atomic paired group to match the 1658-game packet and the mirror. Difficulty deliberately left at 6/10 rather than copying the mirror's 8/10, which is the inverse side.
